tier_reason: The benchmark repo (tweedegolf/async-rtos-showdown) holds the Embassy (rust/), RTIC (rtic/) and FreeRTOS (c/) firmware, but neither it nor the Embassy README carries a single number; the figures exist only in the tweedegolf.nl blog post, which is unreachable here (DNS ENOTFOUND), and two WebSearch passes returned no figures even in snippets, so the entry stays at D.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: Rust (rust/Cargo.toml): nightly toolchain (feature type_alias_impl_trait), [profile.release] opt-level = 3, lto = true, codegen-units = 1, incremental = false, debug = true (debug info only), embassy and embassy-stm32 from git master of early 2022. C (c/.cproject, STM32CubeIDE 1.8.0, MCU ARM GCC arm-none-eabi-): Release configuration C optimization -O3 with -g0 and no LTO (C++ option -Os, unused by this C project); the Debug configuration leaves the optimization level at the IDE default. The repo does not say which C configuration was measured, and no compiler versions are stated for either side.
corrections.stars_or_usage: embassy-rs/embassy: 9.9k stars, 1.7k forks; tweedegolf/async-rtos-showdown: 18 stars, 2 forks, 3 commits (2022-01-04 to 2022-02-17)
corrections.workload: Same toy firmware on a NUCLEO-F446ZE at 180 MHz in Embassy, RTIC and FreeRTOS (CMSIS-RTOS v2 over ST HAL): one task blinks an LED every 100 ms, a button task waits on the EXTI13 user-button interrupt and toggles GPIO PG1 (interrupt-to-task latency read on an oscilloscope), formats a 32-byte message and queues it to a UART writer task. Per search-result summaries (blog unreachable), the post compares interrupt latency, program size, static RAM and ease of programming.
corrections.caveats: Tier D because no number could be read from any opened page; the blog post with the figures (tweedegolf.nl/en/blog/65/async-rust-vs-rtos-showdown) was unreachable (DNS ENOTFOUND), as were the zeli.app and hn.svelte.dev mirrors. Secondary search summaries (snippet only) say Embassy used less RAM and flash but FreeRTOS had better interrupt latency, so 'faster' is not established; Reddit r/embedded and Hacker News commenters said worst-case latency was not measured, only the standard deviation, and flagged the C app's static RAM figure. The verifier read the C side and found it does not do the same work as the Rust side: (1) the UART writer uses blocking polled HAL_UART_Transmit, while Embassy writes over DMA asynchronously; (2) the C message formatting uses newlib snprintf (configUSE_NEWLIB_REENTRANT 1), while Rust uses core::fmt into an ArrayString; (3) the C button task's 'only react to falling edges' block sets the same RTSR/FTSR bits as the rising-edge block (EXTI->RTSR |= pin; EXTI->FTSR &= ~pin), so the C firmware waits on two rising edges and never on a falling edge; (4) the EXTI path goes through the ST HAL callback and the CMSIS-RTOS v2 wrapper (osThreadFlagsSet) instead of native FreeRTOS calls. FreeRTOSConfig.h is the untuned CubeMX default: a static 15360-byte heap (configTOTAL_HEAP_SIZE), three 512-byte task stacks, trace facility, software timers, recursive mutexes and generic task selection (configUSE_PORT_OPTIMISED_TASK_SELECTION 0) all on, which inflates the C side's static RAM and flash. Build settings are not equivalent: the Rust side uses LTO and codegen-units = 1 at opt-level 3, the C Release build -O3 without LTO (larger code than -Os), and the repo does not say whether the Debug or Release C build was measured. The showdown repo is a Feb 2022 snapshot built on Embassy master of that date, so the result predates four years of Embassy and FreeRTOS changes. A cooperative executor versus a preemptive RTOS is not a like-for-like scheduling comparison. The only claim in the embassy repo itself is a README sentence linking the blog.

notes: Confirm at D: Embassy is notable (9.9k stars) and the comparison code is public, but no numbers were reachable and secondary summaries say FreeRTOS won interrupt latency. Shortcomings to record: no numbers reachable (blog blocked); C baseline is untuned CubeMX FreeRTOS behind the CMSIS-RTOS v2 wrapper and ST HAL with a 15 KB static heap, blocking polled UART vs Embassy DMA, newlib snprintf vs core::fmt, a falling-edge EXTI configuration bug, and no LTO on the C side against LTO plus codegen-units = 1 on the Rust side; worst-case latency not measured; 2022 snapshot. If the blog is ever reached, the tier could rise only to C or B, not A, because the C and Rust firmware do different work and the measured C configuration and compiler versions are unstated.
